short_name: Aircraft-Aircraft power plant-Engine bleed air system
rationale: Post-accident testing and bench work pointed to a compressor bleed valve malfunction (air leakage around the piston, slow closure), the same bleed valve failure mode that caused power loss and surging in the cited precedents.

The No. 4 connecting rod failed and oil was lost on a Cessna 210 engine that had gone decades without overhaul, and comparable precedents attribute such connecting rod failures to lubrication loss, clamping force loss, or bearing failure in reciprocating engines.

Dark night, minimal ground lighting over an unlit wetland, and a rapid descent before impact match precedents where night conditions without visual references led to spatial disorientation and perception/orientation errors.
Crew decision to continue an approach and land despite wind data exceeding limits, including reliance on incomplete wind information, parallels precedent accidents where crews should not have landed.

Gusting crosswind exceeding the airplane's demonstrated crosswind capability was the key environmental condition in comparable precedent accidents, matching the 19 kt steady and 23 kt gusting crosswind here.

short_name: Aircraft-Aircraft power plant-Engine fuel and control
rationale: Loose fuel line fittings in the fuel metering/delivery path caused fuel leakage and loss of engine power in several precedent accidents, matching the loose fuel line at the throttle body in this incident.
Multiple sedating medications (diphenhydramine, gabapentin, venlafaxine) detected at high levels likely impaired the pilot's physical and cognitive performance, as in precedent cases.

The pilot's failure to apply carburetor heat in conditions favorable for serious carburetor icing, as in the cited precedents, is the most likely action-level cause here since the pilot stated he did not use carburetor heat before power loss.
Temperature and dew point of about 80°F and 71°F placed the airplane in the serious carburetor icing range at glide power, matching the atmospheric conditions in the precedent accidents.
The airplane impacted sloping mountainous terrain in the Cascades area, and precedent accidents cite flight over mountainous terrain as a factor in the loss of control.

The pilot had only a private certificate with no weight-shift experience logged beyond the aircraft type, and precedent analyses cite limited weight-shift experience as contributing to loss of control.

short_name: Aircraft-Aircraft power plant-Engine fuel and control
rationale: Contamination of the fuel injector servo regulator section with fuel/oil or debris restricted fuel flow, causing loss of power during takeoff, matching this engine fuel and control failure.

The right engine lost power because the throttle arm and control lever were loose and the throttle linkage was not securely connected, a mechanism matching the engine-control disconnection in the precedent accidents.
Loosened and unretained gear attachment nuts/bolts that went unnoticed suggest maintenance inspection and hardware security checks were inadequate, as in precedent gear trunnion cases.
The temperature and dew point conditions favored serious carburetor icing at glide or descent power, as in the cited precedents where icing was the environmental condition behind the power loss.
The rudder and its hinge/post are empennage structure, and the fatigue fracture of the rudder hinge and post is a structural failure of that component.
Overload failures of the empennage and wings in an in-flight breakup are consistent with structural exceedance of the airframe, as in these precedents.
The airplane impacted steep, densely forested terrain at 45 to 60 degrees while flying through canyon walls up to 5,500 ft, which is the mountainous terrain factor cited in the precedents.
The fractured axle attachment bolts and separated right main wheel assembly point to a landing gear system failure, consistent with multiple precedent main gear bolt and spring overstress failures.
The pilot's turns over dark water with no visible horizon, followed by a loss of control, match precedents where spatial disorientation (perception/orientation illusion) was the probable cause.

The accident airplane's carburetor air inlet hose, improper part with thinner single-ply wall, collapsed and restricted airflow to the engine causing power loss, a mechanism matching the 2013 and 2019 precedents where the air inlet duct or heat valve detachment restricted the carburetor air supply.
The reported temperature and dew point were charted as conducive to serious carburetor icing at glide power, which is the environmental condition behind the icing risk.

The missing and loose turbocharger oil line fitting bolts after a recent oil-change maintenance visit match precedents where improper maintenance torquing of oil line fittings caused oil starvation and power loss.

The No. 2 intake valve failure (keeper dislodgement, neck fracture, piston damage, and power loss) is an engine internal valve train failure, and comparable precedents attribute partial power loss to intake or exhaust valve failures within the engine.

Asymmetric thrust and the difficulty of maintaining climb and directional control after an engine loss at low altitude are cognitive and control challenges precedent accidents attributed to pilot handling.

Fuel pressure dropping to zero shortly after takeoff, the right tank exhausted, and the selector left on the right tank point to fuel system starvation, a fuel system cause in the precedent accidents.

The pilot observed low fuel gauge indications on the return flight but did not manage consumption or fuel quantity, consistent with precedents where failure to monitor and manage fuel use caused fuel exhaustion.

The alternator/battery electrical power supply degraded during flight, with voltage falling steadily until the fuel pumps and ignition lost power, matching precedent electrical-system failures causing engine power loss.

rationale: Precedent accidents show in-flight engine fires from fuel injector or fuel nozzle installation and leak problems in the engine fuel control and delivery system, which is the mechanism implicated by the fire concentrated at cylinders 3 and 5 after injector removal and reinstallation.
The pilot's improper use of the mixture control equipment, contrary to the POH checklist, is the operational error that the precedent accidents identified as causing detonation or power loss.

Precedent probable causes repeatedly attribute controlled flight into terrain to a pilot's decision to continue VFR flight into instrument meteorological conditions over mountainous terrain, matching the decision-making issue implied by the packet's weather and terrain facts.

This reciprocating engine (Aeronca 11AC) suffered a crankshaft fatigue fracture leading to total power loss, the same failure mode recorded against reciprocating engine components in the precedent accidents.
The partial power loss after takeoff was traced to fuel injector obstruction, a fuel system component blockage similar to the precedent where a blocked injector caused partial power loss on takeoff.

Pilot likely became spatially disoriented after entering IMC with cloud base about 100 ft agl and a loss of control, which precedent accidents tie to spatial disorientation (perception/orientation/illusion).
Gusty tailwind conditions (12 kt wind from 120 degrees with gusts to 17 kt, near the 10 kt tailwind limit) were a contributing environmental factor in precedent overrun accidents.

rationale: The partial loss of power after takeoff was traced to fuel injection servo contamination and related fuel-system faults in several precedent accidents, matching the updraft-mounted RSA-5 servo contamination described in this packet.

Precedent probable causes identify the failure to properly perform required blade inspections, including the pilot's preflight inspection, as a factor in cracks that went undetected, consistent with the missed crack on this blade.

short_name: Aircraft-Aircraft power plant-Engine fuel and control
rationale: The engine power loss was attributed to carburetor ice in a carburetor fuel-metering system, and the mogas/ethanol and volatility discussion explains why automotive fuel increases carburetor icing risk.

The pilot's failure to apply carburetor heat during a prolonged reduced-power period in conditions conducive to carburetor icing is a decision/information-processing lapse, as in the precedent accidents where omitted carburetor heat led to power loss.
The pilot's fuel quantity planning and consumption estimate were inadequate, leading to fuel exhaustion, which matches prior accidents attributed to inadequate preflight fuel planning.

Improper maintenance of valve train and rocker arm adjustment (incorrect No. 4 rocker adjustment and clearance not maintained) is a maintenance task performance issue matching precedent cases of improper maintenance causing rocker arm related power loss.

The forward pressure bulkhead canted web fatigue cracking with stress corrosion contribution in a Lockheed 382 mirrors the prior 2016 rupture, establishing the fuselage/pressure bulkhead structural failure as the finding.

The pilot's decision to continue VFR flight into deteriorating night conditions with low ceilings and no horizon, documented in several precedents, parallels the low-ceiling night descent here, which is a decision/information processing failure.
Low cloud ceilings and reduced visibility at night were present near the accident site, as in the precedents where such conditions drove the accident sequence.
The cabin entry door opened in flight after takeoff, as in multiple precedents where an unsecured or opening door was the central fact leading to loss of control.
Precedents show pilots' attention diverted by an opening door during initial climb, which may apply to the pilot's loss of control here.
The pilot's attention was diverted by the open baggage door during takeoff, which precedent associates with loss of airplane control after takeoff.

The pilot's failure to apply carburetor heat before closing the throttle in icing-conducive conditions is the central action error, matching multiple precedents where the same omission caused power loss on approach or descent.
